and spin-up time. There's also a full parts list with spares and rebuild time.

anything that's rigid bits, hinges, sliders and motors: twin flippers, a
rolling ball, a six-legged walker, a full-body spinner, axes, ram spikes,
lifters, clampers…

- **Parts:** box, wedge, flat plate, bar, cylinder/disc, cone, sphere, capsule,
  or a custom convex hull from your own points. Each one has a material
  (aluminium, mild steel, hardened steel, titanium, HDPE, polycarbonate,
  rubber, PTFE, plywood) and is either solid or a hollow shell with a wall
  thickness. Its size, position, rotation and shape offset are all editable.
- **Joints:** every part is *fixed* to its parent, on a *hinge* (with an axis and
  optional angle limits), or on a *slider* (with travel limits).

  steering, weapon buttons 1–4 (held or toggled), or the walking gait
  (stride side, phase, swing or lift).

  ballast.

  leg with hip and knee servos, an axe, a spinner or a ram spike), mirror a
  part with everything on it to the other side, duplicate, move it onto

e## The Garage

Robots are **trees of parts joined by joints**, so you can build almost
anything that's rigid bits, hinges, sliders and motors: twin flippers, a
rolling ball, a six-legged walker, a full-body spinner, axes, ram spikes,
lifters, clampers…

- **Parts:** box, wedge, flat plate, bar, cylinder/disc, cone, sphere, capsule,
  or a custom convex hull from your own points. Each one has a material
  (aluminium, mild steel, hardened steel, titanium, HDPE, polycarbonate,
  rubber, PTFE, plywood) and is either solid or a hollow shell with a wall
  thickness. Its size, position, rotation and shape offset are all editable.
- **Joints:** every part is *fixed* to its parent, on a *hinge* (with an axis and
  optional angle limits), or on a *slider* (with travel limits).
- **Actuators** on any hinge or slider:
  - a **DC motor** through a gearbox, for wheels, spinners and drums;
  - a **pneumatic ram**, with your choice of ram, valve and pressure, for
    flippers, lifters, axes and spikes;
  - a **servo**, which holds positions, for legs, clamps and steering.
- **Wiring:** any actuator can follow the left or right drive, throttle,
  steering, weapon buttons 1–4 (held or toggled), or the walking gait
  (stride side, phase, swing or lift).
- **Internals:** batteries (in parallel), gas bottles (one shared supply) and
  ballast.
- **Tools:** add from a parts menu (including ready-wired assemblies such as a
  leg with hip and knee servos, an axe, a spinner or a ram spike), mirror a
  part with everything on it to the other side, duplicate, move it onto
  another part, or remove it. Click a part in the 3D view to select it.

Stats update as you build: weight, cost, drive (top speed and pushing force
for wheeled robots), battery life, and each weapon's force or stored energy
and spin-up time. There's also a full parts list with spares and rebuild time.
**Scrutineering** checks weight class, budget, size, parts below the floor,
voltage against each motor, gas for the pneumatics, wiring and battery life.
The **test bay** behind the editor lets you drive the robot against a
crash-test dummy, with live telemetry for every joint.

Starter robots: Wedgehog (wedge), Flipside (flipper), Whirlwind (undercutter),
Twin Terror (two flippers), Orb (pendulum-drive sphere), Arachnid (six-legged
walker) and Gyrodisc (full-body spinner). Saved robots appear on the fight
select screen. Designs are plain JSON, so you can copy one out to share it or
paste one in; old saves are upgraded automatically.

and spin-up time. There's also a full parts list with spares and rebuild time.
**Scrutineering** checks weight class, budget, size, parts below the floor,
voltage against each motor, gas for the pneumatics, wiring and battery life.
The **test bay** behind the editor lets you drive the robot against a
crash-test dummy, with live telemetry for every joint.

Starter robots: Wedgehog (wedge), Flipside (flipper), Whirlwind (undercutter),
Twin Terror (two flippers), Orb (pendulum-drive sphere), Arachnid (six-legged
walker) and Gyrodisc (full-body spinner). Saved robots appear on the fight
select screen. Designs are plain JSON, so you can copy one out to share it or
paste one in; old saves are upgraded automatically.


## The Garage

Robots are **trees of parts joined by joints**, so you can build almost
anything that's rigid bits, hinges, sliders and motors: twin flippers, a
rolling ball, a six-legged walker, a full-body spinner, axes, ram spikes,
lifters, clampers…

- **Parts:** box, wedge, flat plate, bar, cylinder/disc, cone, sphere, capsule,
  or a custom convex hull from your own points. Each one has a material
  (aluminium, mild steel, hardened steel, titanium, HDPE, polycarbonate,
  rubber, PTFE, plywood) and is either solid or a hollow shell with a wall
  thickness. Its size, position, rotation and shape offset are all editable.
- **Joints:** every part is *fixed* to its parent, on a *hinge* (with an axis and
  optional angle limits), or on a *slider* (with travel limits).
- **Actuators** on any hinge or slider:
  - a **DC motor** through a gearbox, for wheels, spinners and drums;
  - a **pneumatic ram**, with your choice of ram, valve and pressure, for
    flippers, lifters, axes and spikes;
  - a **servo**, which holds positions, for legs, clamps and steering.
- **Wiring:** any actuator can follow the left or right drive, throttle,
  steering, weapon buttons 1–4 (held or toggled), or the walking gait
  (stride side, phase, swing or lift).
- **Internals:** batteries (in parallel), gas bottles (one shared supply) and
  ballast.
- **Tools:** add from a parts menu (including ready-wired assemblies such as a
  leg with hip and knee servos, an axe, a spinner or a ram spike), mirror a
  part with everything on it to the other side, duplicate, move it onto
  another part, or remove it. Click a part in the 3D view to select it.

Stats update as you build: weight, cost, drive (top speed and pushing force
for wheeled robots), battery life, and each weapon's force or stored energy
and spin-up time. There's also a full parts list with spares and rebuild time.
**Scrutineering** checks weight class, budget, size, parts below the floor,
voltage against each motor, gas for the pneumatics, wiring and battery life.
The **test bay** behind the editor lets you drive the robot against a
crash-test dummy, with live telemetry for every joint.

Starter robots: Wedgehog (wedge), Flipside (flipper), Whirlwind (undercutter),
Twin Terror (two flippers), Orb (pendulum-drive sphere), Arachnid (six-legged
walker) and Gyrodisc (full-body spinner). Saved robots appear on the fight
select screen. Designs are plain JSON, so you can copy one out to share it or
paste one in; old saves are upgraded automatically.

t## The Garage

Robots are **trees of parts joined by joints**, so you can build almost
anything that's rigid bits, hinges, sliders and motors: twin flippers, a
rolling ball, a six-legged walker, a full-body spinner, axes, ram spikes,
lifters, clampers…

- **Parts:** box, wedge, flat plate, bar, cylinder/disc, cone, sphere, capsule,
  or a custom convex hull from your own points. Each one has a material
  (aluminium, mild steel, hardened steel, titanium, HDPE, polycarbonate,
  rubber, PTFE, plywood) and is either solid or a hollow shell with a wall
  thickness. Its size, position, rotation and shape offset are all editable.
- **Joints:** every part is *fixed* to its parent, on a *hinge* (with an axis and
  optional angle limits), or on a *slider* (with travel limits).
- **Actuators** on any hinge or slider:
  - a **DC motor** through a gearbox, for wheels, spinners and drums;
  - a **pneumatic ram**, with your choice of ram, valve and pressure, for
    flippers, lifters, axes and spikes;
  - a **servo**, which holds positions, for legs, clamps and steering.
- **Wiring:** any actuator can follow the left or right drive, throttle,
  steering, weapon buttons 1–4 (held or toggled), or the walking gait
  (stride side, phase, swing or lift).
- **Internals:** batteries (in parallel), gas bottles (one shared supply) and
  ballast.
- **Tools:** add from a parts menu (including ready-wired assemblies such as a
  leg with hip and knee servos, an axe, a spinner or a ram spike), mirror a
  part with everything on it to the other side, duplicate, move it onto
  another part, or remove it. Click a part in the 3D view to select it.

Stats update as you build: weight, cost, drive (top speed and pushing force
for wheeled robots), battery life, and each weapon's force or stored energy
and spin-up time. There's also a full parts list with spares and rebuild time.
**Scrutineering** checks weight class, budget, size, parts below the floor,
voltage against each motor, gas for the pneumatics, wiring and battery life.

o## The Garage

Robots are **trees of parts joined by joints**, so you can build almost
anything that's rigid bits, hinges, sliders and motors: twin flippers, a
rolling ball, a six-legged walker, a full-body spinner, axes, ram spikes,
lifters, clampers…

- **Parts:** box, wedge, flat plate, bar, cylinder/disc, cone, sphere, capsule,
  or a custom convex hull from your own points. Each one has a material
  (aluminium, mild steel, hardened steel, titanium, HDPE, polycarbonate,
  rubber, PTFE, plywood) and is either solid or a hollow shell with a wall
  thickness. Its size, position, rotation and shape offset are all editable.
- **Joints:** every part is *fixed* to its parent, on a *hinge* (with an axis and
  optional angle limits), or on a *slider* (with travel limits).
- **Actuators** on any hinge or slider:
  - a **DC motor** through a gearbox, for wheels, spinners and drums;
  - a **pneumatic ram**, with your choice of ram, valve and pressure, for
    flippers, lifters, axes and spikes;
  - a **servo**, which holds positions, for legs, clamps and steering.
- **Wiring:** any actuator can follow the left or right drive, throttle,
  steering, weapon buttons 1–4 (held or toggled), or the walking gait
  (stride side, phase, swing or lift).
- **Internals:** batteries (in parallel), gas bottles (one shared supply) and
  ballast.
- **Tools:** add from a parts menu (including ready-wired assemblies such as a
  leg with hip and knee servos, an axe, a spinner or a ram spike), mirror a
  part with everything on it to the other side, duplicate, move it onto
  another part, or remove it. Click a part in the 3D view to select it.

Stats update as you build: weight, cost, drive (top speed and pushing force
for wheeled robots), battery life, and each weapon's force or stored energy
and spin-up time. There's also a full parts list with spares and rebuild time.
**Scrutineering** checks weight class, budget, size, parts below the floor,
voltage against each motor, gas for the pneumatics, wiring and battery life.
The **test bay** behind the editor lets you drive the robot against a
crash-test dummy, with live telemetry for every joint.

Starter robots: Wedgehog (wedge), Flipside (flipper), Whirlwind (undercutter),
Twin Terror (two flippers), Orb (pendulum-drive sphere), Arachnid (six-legged
walker) and Gyrodisc (full-body spinner). Saved robots appear on the fight
select screen. Designs are plain JSON, so you can copy one out to share it or
paste one in; old saves are upgraded automatically.

- **Parts:** box, wedge, flat plate, bar, cylinder/disc, cone, sphere, capsule,
  or a custom convex hull from your own points. Each one has a material
  (aluminium, mild steel, hardened steel, titanium, HDPE, polycarbonate,
  rubber, PTFE, plywood) and is either solid or a hollow shell with a wall
  thickness. Its size, position, rotation and shape offset are all editable.
- **Joints:** every part is *fixed* to its parent, on a *hinge* (with an axis and
  optional angle limits), or on a *slider* (with travel limits).
- **Actuators** on any hinge or slider:
  - a **DC motor** through a gearbox, for wheels, spinners and drums;
  - a **pneumatic ram**, with your choice of ram, valve and pressure, for
    flippers, lifters, axes and spikes;
  - a **servo**, which holds positions, for legs, clamps and steering.
- **Wiring:** any actuator can follow the left or right drive, throttle,
  steering, weapon buttons 1–4 (held or toggled), or the walking gait
  (stride side, phase, swing or lift).
- **Internals:** batteries (in parallel), gas bottles (one shared supply) and
  ballast.
- **Tools:** add from a parts menu (including ready-wired assemblies such as a
  leg with hip and knee servos, an axe, a spinner or a ram spike), mirror a
  part with everything on it to the other side, duplicate, move it onto
  another part, or remove it. Click a part in the 3D view to select it.

Stats update as you build: weight, cost, drive (top speed and pushing force
for wheeled robots), battery life, and each weapon's force or stored energy
and spin-up time. There's also a full parts list with spares and rebuild time.
**Scrutineering** checks weight class, budget, size, parts below the floor,
voltage against each motor, gas for the pneumatics, wiring and battery life.
The **test bay** behind the editor lets you drive the robot against a
crash-test dummy, with live telemetry for every joint.

Starter robots: Wedgehog (wedge), Flipside (flipper), Whirlwind (undercutter),

walker) and Gyrodisc (full-body spinner). Saved robots appear on the fight

and spin-up time. There's also a full parts list with spares and rebuild time.
**Scrutineering** checks weight class, budget, size, parts below the floor,
voltage against each motor, gas for the pneumatics, wiring and battery life.
The **test bay** behind the editor lets you drive the robot against a
crash-test dummy, with live telemetry for every joint.

Starter robots: Wedgehog (wedge), Flipside (flipper), Whirlwind (undercutter),
Twin Terror (two flippers), Orb (pendulum-drive sphere), Arachnid (six-legged
walker) and Gyrodisc (full-body spinner). Saved robots appear on the fight
select screen. Designs are plain JSON, so you can copy one out to share it or
paste one in; old saves are upgraded automatically.

 ## The Garage

Robots are **trees of parts joined by joints**, so you can build almost
anything that's rigid bits, hinges, sliders and motors: twin flippers, a
rolling ball, a six-legged walker, a full-body spinner, axes, ram spikes,
lifters, clampers…

- **Parts:** box, wedge, flat plate, bar, cylinder/disc, cone, sphere, capsule,
  or a custom convex hull from your own points. Each one has a material
  (aluminium, mild steel, hardened steel, titanium, HDPE, polycarbonate,
  rubber, PTFE, plywood) and is either solid or a hollow shell with a wall
  thickness. Its size, position, rotation and shape offset are all editable.
- **Joints:** every part is *fixed* to its parent, on a *hinge* (with an axis and
  optional angle limits), or on a *slider* (with travel limits).
- **Actuators** on any hinge or slider:
  - a **DC motor** through a gearbox, for wheels, spinners and drums;
  - a **pneumatic ram**, with your choice of ram, valve and pressure, for
    flippers, lifters, axes and spikes;
  - a **servo**, which holds positions, for legs, clamps and steering.
- **Wiring:** any actuator can follow the left or right drive, throttle,
  steering, weapon buttons 1–4 (held or toggled), or the walking gait
  (stride side, phase, swing or lift).
- **Internals:** batteries (in parallel), gas bottles (one shared supply) and
  ballast.
- **Tools:** add from a parts menu (including ready-wired assemblies such as a
  leg with hip and knee servos, an axe, a spinner or a ram spike), mirror a
  part with everything on it to the other side, duplicate, move it onto
  another part, or remove it. Click a part in the 3D view to select it.

Stats update as you build: weight, cost, drive (top speed and pushing force
for wheeled robots), battery life, and each weapon's force or stored energy
and spin-up time. There's also a full parts list with spares and rebuild time.
**Scrutineering** checks weight class, budget, size, parts below the floor,
voltage against each motor, gas for the pneumatics, wiring and battery life.
The **test bay** behind the editor lets you drive the robot against a
crash-test dummy, with live telemetry for every joint.

paste one in; old saves are upgraded automatically.

- **Parts:** box, wedge, flat plate, bar, cylinder/disc, cone, sphere, capsule,
  or a custom convex hull from your own points. Each one has a material
  (aluminium, mild steel, hardened steel, titanium, HDPE, polycarbonate,
  rubber, PTFE, plywood) and is either solid or a hollow shell with a wall
  thickness. Its size, position, rotation and shape offset are all editable.

b## The Garage

Robots are **trees of parts joined by joints**, so you can build almost
anything that's rigid bits, hinges, sliders and motors: twin flippers, a
rolling ball, a six-legged walker, a full-body spinner, axes, ram spikes,
lifters, clampers…

- **Parts:** box, wedge, flat plate, bar, cylinder/disc, cone, sphere, capsule,
  or a custom convex hull from your own points. Each one has a material
  (aluminium, mild steel, hardened steel, titanium, HDPE, polycarbonate,
  rubber, PTFE, plywood) and is either solid or a hollow shell with a wall
  thickness. Its size, position, rotation and shape offset are all editable.
- **Joints:** every part is *fixed* to its parent, on a *hinge* (with an axis and
  optional angle limits), or on a *slider* (with travel limits).
- **Actuators** on any hinge or slider:
  - a **DC motor** through a gearbox, for wheels, spinners and drums;
  - a **pneumatic ram**, with your choice of ram, valve and pressure, for
    flippers, lifters, axes and spikes;
  - a **servo**, which holds positions, for legs, clamps and steering.
- **Wiring:** any actuator can follow the left or right drive, throttle,
  steering, weapon buttons 1–4 (held or toggled), or the walking gait
  (stride side, phase, swing or lift).
- **Internals:** batteries (in parallel), gas bottles (one shared supply) and
  ballast.
- **Tools:** add from a parts menu (including ready-wired assemblies such as a
  leg with hip and knee servos, an axe, a spinner or a ram spike), mirror a
  part with everything on it to the other side, duplicate, move it onto
  another part, or remove it. Click a part in the 3D view to select it.

Stats update as you build: weight, cost, drive (top speed and pushing force
for wheeled robots), battery life, and each weapon's force or stored energy
and spin-up time. There's also a full parts list with spares and rebuild time.
**Scrutineering** checks weight class, budget, size, parts below the floor,
voltage against each motor, gas for the pneumatics, wiring and battery life.
The **test bay** behind the editor lets you drive the robot against a
crash-test dummy, with live telemetry for every joint.

Starter robots: Wedgehog (wedge), Flipside (flipper), Whirlwind (undercutter),
Twin Terror (two flippers), Orb (pendulum-drive sphere), Arachnid (six-legged
walker) and Gyrodisc (full-body spinner). Saved robots appear on the fight
select screen. Designs are plain JSON, so you can copy one out to share it or
paste one in; old saves are upgraded automatically.

  or a custom convex hull from your own points. Each one has a material

  rubber, PTFE, plywood) and is either solid or a hollow shell with a wall

  - a **DC motor** through a gearbox, for wheels, spinners and drums;

r## The Garage

Robots are **trees of parts joined by joints**, so you can build almost
anything that's rigid bits, hinges, sliders and motors: twin flippers, a
rolling ball, a six-legged walker, a full-body spinner, axes, ram spikes,
lifters, clampers…

- **Parts:** box, wedge, flat plate, bar, cylinder/disc, cone, sphere, capsule,
  or a custom convex hull from your own points. Each one has a material
  (aluminium, mild steel, hardened steel, titanium, HDPE, polycarbonate,
  rubber, PTFE, plywood) and is either solid or a hollow shell with a wall
  thickness. Its size, position, rotation and shape offset are all editable.
- **Joints:** every part is *fixed* to its parent, on a *hinge* (with an axis and
  optional angle limits), or on a *slider* (with travel limits).
- **Actuators** on any hinge or slider:
  - a **DC motor** through a gearbox, for wheels, spinners and drums;
  - a **pneumatic ram**, with your choice of ram, valve and pressure, for
    flippers, lifters, axes and spikes;
  - a **servo**, which holds positions, for legs, clamps and steering.
- **Wiring:** any actuator can follow the left or right drive, throttle,
  steering, weapon buttons 1–4 (held or toggled), or the walking gait
  (stride side, phase, swing or lift).
- **Internals:** batteries (in parallel), gas bottles (one shared supply) and
  ballast.
- **Tools:** add from a parts menu (including ready-wired assemblies such as a
  leg with hip and knee servos, an axe, a spinner or a ram spike), mirror a
  part with everything on it to the other side, duplicate, move it onto
  another part, or remove it. Click a part in the 3D view to select it.

Stats update as you build: weight, cost, drive (top speed and pushing force
for wheeled robots), battery life, and each weapon's force or stored energy
and spin-up time. There's also a full parts list with spares and rebuild time.

b## The Garage

Robots are **trees of parts joined by joints**, so you can build almost
anything that's rigid bits, hinges, sliders and motors: twin flippers, a
rolling ball, a six-legged walker, a full-body spinner, axes, ram spikes,
lifters, clampers…

- **Parts:** box, wedge, flat plate, bar, cylinder/disc, cone, sphere, capsule,
  or a custom convex hull from your own points. Each one has a material
  (aluminium, mild steel, hardened steel, titanium, HDPE, polycarbonate,
  rubber, PTFE, plywood) and is either solid or a hollow shell with a wall
  thickness. Its size, position, rotation and shape offset are all editable.
- **Joints:** every part is *fixed* to its parent, on a *hinge* (with an axis and
  optional angle limits), or on a *slider* (with travel limits).
- **Actuators** on any hinge or slider:
  - a **DC motor** through a gearbox, for wheels, spinners and drums;
  - a **pneumatic ram**, with your choice of ram, valve and pressure, for
    flippers, lifters, axes and spikes;
  - a **servo**, which holds positions, for legs, clamps and steering.
- **Wiring:** any actuator can follow the left or right drive, throttle,
  steering, weapon buttons 1–4 (held or toggled), or the walking gait
  (stride side, phase, swing or lift).
- **Internals:** batteries (in parallel), gas bottles (one shared supply) and
  ballast.
- **Tools:** add from a parts menu (including ready-wired assemblies such as a
  leg with hip and knee servos, an axe, a spinner or a ram spike), mirror a
  part with everything on it to the other side, duplicate, move it onto
  another part, or remove it. Click a part in the 3D view to select it.

Stats update as you build: weight, cost, drive (top speed and pushing force
for wheeled robots), battery life, and each weapon's force or stored energy
and spin-up time. There's also a full parts list with spares and rebuild time.
**Scrutineering** checks weight class, budget, size, parts below the floor,

e## The Garage

Robots are **trees of parts joined by joints**, so you can build almost
anything that's rigid bits, hinges, sliders and motors: twin flippers, a
rolling ball, a six-legged walker, a full-body spinner, axes, ram spikes,
lifters, clampers…

- **Parts:** box, wedge, flat plate, bar, cylinder/disc, cone, sphere, capsule,
  or a custom convex hull from your own points. Each one has a material
  (aluminium, mild steel, hardened steel, titanium, HDPE, polycarbonate,
  rubber, PTFE, plywood) and is either solid or a hollow shell with a wall
  thickness. Its size, position, rotation and shape offset are all editable.
- **Joints:** every part is *fixed* to its parent, on a *hinge* (with an axis and
  optional angle limits), or on a *slider* (with travel limits).
- **Actuators** on any hinge or slider:
  - a **DC motor** through a gearbox, for wheels, spinners and drums;
  - a **pneumatic ram**, with your choice of ram, valve and pressure, for
    flippers, lifters, axes and spikes;
  - a **servo**, which holds positions, for legs, clamps and steering.
- **Wiring:** any actuator can follow the left or right drive, throttle,
  steering, weapon buttons 1–4 (held or toggled), or the walking gait
  (stride side, phase, swing or lift).
- **Internals:** batteries (in parallel), gas bottles (one shared supply) and
  ballast.
- **Tools:** add from a parts menu (including ready-wired assemblies such as a
  leg with hip and knee servos, an axe, a spinner or a ram spike), mirror a
  part with everything on it to the other side, duplicate, move it onto
  another part, or remove it. Click a part in the 3D view to select it.

Stats update as you build: weight, cost, drive (top speed and pushing force
for wheeled robots), battery life, and each weapon's force or stored energy
and spin-up time. There's also a full parts list with spares and rebuild time.
**Scrutineering** checks weight class, budget, size, parts below the floor,
voltage against each motor, gas for the pneumatics, wiring and battery life.
The **test bay** behind the editor lets you drive the robot against a
crash-test dummy, with live telemetry for every joint.

Starter robots: Wedgehog (wedge), Flipside (flipper), Whirlwind (undercutter),
Twin Terror (two flippers), Orb (pendulum-drive sphere), Arachnid (six-legged
walker) and Gyrodisc (full-body spinner). Saved robots appear on the fight
select screen. Designs are plain JSON, so you can copy one out to share it or
paste one in; old saves are upgraded automatically.

:## The Garage

Robots are **trees of parts joined by joints**, so you can build almost
anything that's rigid bits, hinges, sliders and motors: twin flippers, a
rolling ball, a six-legged walker, a full-body spinner, axes, ram spikes,
lifters, clampers…

- **Parts:** box, wedge, flat plate, bar, cylinder/disc, cone, sphere, capsule,
  or a custom convex hull from your own points. Each one has a material
  (aluminium, mild steel, hardened steel, titanium, HDPE, polycarbonate,
  rubber, PTFE, plywood) and is either solid or a hollow shell with a wall
  thickness. Its size, position, rotation and shape offset are all editable.
- **Joints:** every part is *fixed* to its parent, on a *hinge* (with an axis and
  optional angle limits), or on a *slider* (with travel limits).
- **Actuators** on any hinge or slider:
  - a **DC motor** through a gearbox, for wheels, spinners and drums;
  - a **pneumatic ram**, with your choice of ram, valve and pressure, for
    flippers, lifters, axes and spikes;
  - a **servo**, which holds positions, for legs, clamps and steering.
- **Wiring:** any actuator can follow the left or right drive, throttle,
  steering, weapon buttons 1–4 (held or toggled), or the walking gait
  (stride side, phase, swing or lift).
- **Internals:** batteries (in parallel), gas bottles (one shared supply) and
  ballast.
- **Tools:** add from a parts menu (including ready-wired assemblies such as a
  leg with hip and knee servos, an axe, a spinner or a ram spike), mirror a
  part with everything on it to the other side, duplicate, move it onto
  another part, or remove it. Click a part in the 3D view to select it.

Stats update as you build: weight, cost, drive (top speed and pushing force
for wheeled robots), battery life, and each weapon's force or stored energy
and spin-up time. There's also a full parts list with spares and rebuild time.

o## The Garage

Robots are **trees of parts joined by joints**, so you can build almost
anything that's rigid bits, hinges, sliders and motors: twin flippers, a
rolling ball, a six-legged walker, a full-body spinner, axes, ram spikes,
lifters, clampers…

- **Parts:** box, wedge, flat plate, bar, cylinder/disc, cone, sphere, capsule,
  or a custom convex hull from your own points. Each one has a material
  (aluminium, mild steel, hardened steel, titanium, HDPE, polycarbonate,
  rubber, PTFE, plywood) and is either solid or a hollow shell with a wall
  thickness. Its size, position, rotation and shape offset are all editable.
- **Joints:** every part is *fixed* to its parent, on a *hinge* (with an axis and
  optional angle limits), or on a *slider* (with travel limits).
- **Actuators** on any hinge or slider:
  - a **DC motor** through a gearbox, for wheels, spinners and drums;
  - a **pneumatic ram**, with your choice of ram, valve and pressure, for
    flippers, lifters, axes and spikes;
  - a **servo**, which holds positions, for legs, clamps and steering.
- **Wiring:** any actuator can follow the left or right drive, throttle,
  steering, weapon buttons 1–4 (held or toggled), or the walking gait
  (stride side, phase, swing or lift).
- **Internals:** batteries (in parallel), gas bottles (one shared supply) and
  ballast.
- **Tools:** add from a parts menu (including ready-wired assemblies such as a
  leg with hip and knee servos, an axe, a spinner or a ram spike), mirror a
  part with everything on it to the other side, duplicate, move it onto
  another part, or remove it. Click a part in the 3D view to select it.

Stats update as you build: weight, cost, drive (top speed and pushing force
for wheeled robots), battery life, and each weapon's force or stored energy
and spin-up time. There's also a full parts list with spares and rebuild time.
**Scrutineering** checks weight class, budget, size, parts below the floor,

 ## The Garage

Robots are **trees of parts joined by joints**, so you can build almost
anything that's rigid bits, hinges, sliders and motors: twin flippers, a
rolling ball, a six-legged walker, a full-body spinner, axes, ram spikes,
lifters, clampers…

- **Parts:** box, wedge, flat plate, bar, cylinder/disc, cone, sphere, capsule,
  or a custom convex hull from your own points. Each one has a material
  (aluminium, mild steel, hardened steel, titanium, HDPE, polycarbonate,
  rubber, PTFE, plywood) and is either solid or a hollow shell with a wall
  thickness. Its size, position, rotation and shape offset are all editable.
- **Joints:** every part is *fixed* to its parent, on a *hinge* (with an axis and
  optional angle limits), or on a *slider* (with travel limits).
- **Actuators** on any hinge or slider:
  - a **DC motor** through a gearbox, for wheels, spinners and drums;
  - a **pneumatic ram**, with your choice of ram, valve and pressure, for
    flippers, lifters, axes and spikes;
  - a **servo**, which holds positions, for legs, clamps and steering.
- **Wiring:** any actuator can follow the left or right drive, throttle,
  steering, weapon buttons 1–4 (held or toggled), or the walking gait
  (stride side, phase, swing or lift).
- **Internals:** batteries (in parallel), gas bottles (one shared supply) and
  ballast.
- **Tools:** add from a parts menu (including ready-wired assemblies such as a
  leg with hip and knee servos, an axe, a spinner or a ram spike), mirror a
  part with everything on it to the other side, duplicate, move it onto
  another part, or remove it. Click a part in the 3D view to select it.

Stats update as you build: weight, cost, drive (top speed and pushing force
for wheeled robots), battery life, and each weapon's force or stored energy
and spin-up time. There's also a full parts list with spares and rebuild time.
**Scrutineering** checks weight class, budget, size, parts below the floor,
voltage against each motor, gas for the pneumatics, wiring and battery life.
The **test bay** behind the editor lets you drive the robot against a
crash-test dummy, with live telemetry for every joint.

Starter robots: Wedgehog (wedge), Flipside (flipper), Whirlwind (undercutter),
Twin Terror (two flippers), Orb (pendulum-drive sphere), Arachnid (six-legged
walker) and Gyrodisc (full-body spinner). Saved robots appear on the fight
select screen. Designs are plain JSON, so you can copy one out to share it or
paste one in; old saves are upgraded automatically.

r## The Garage

Robots are **trees of parts joined by joints**, so you can build almost
anything that's rigid bits, hinges, sliders and motors: twin flippers, a
rolling ball, a six-legged walker, a full-body spinner, axes, ram spikes,
lifters, clampers…

- **Parts:** box, wedge, flat plate, bar, cylinder/disc, cone, sphere, capsule,
  or a custom convex hull from your own points. Each one has a material
  (aluminium, mild steel, hardened steel, titanium, HDPE, polycarbonate,
  rubber, PTFE, plywood) and is either solid or a hollow shell with a wall
  thickness. Its size, position, rotation and shape offset are all editable.
- **Joints:** every part is *fixed* to its parent, on a *hinge* (with an axis and
  optional angle limits), or on a *slider* (with travel limits).
- **Actuators** on any hinge or slider:
  - a **DC motor** through a gearbox, for wheels, spinners and drums;
  - a **pneumatic ram**, with your choice of ram, valve and pressure, for
    flippers, lifters, axes and spikes;
  - a **servo**, which holds positions, for legs, clamps and steering.
- **Wiring:** any actuator can follow the left or right drive, throttle,
  steering, weapon buttons 1–4 (held or toggled), or the walking gait
  (stride side, phase, swing or lift).
- **Internals:** batteries (in parallel), gas bottles (one shared supply) and
  ballast.
- **Tools:** add from a parts menu (including ready-wired assemblies such as a
  leg with hip and knee servos, an axe, a spinner or a ram spike), mirror a
  part with everything on it to the other side, duplicate, move it onto
  another part, or remove it. Click a part in the 3D view to select it.

Stats update as you build: weight, cost, drive (top speed and pushing force
for wheeled robots), battery life, and each weapon's force or stored energy
and spin-up time. There's also a full parts list with spares and rebuild time.

anything that's rigid bits, hinges, sliders and motors: twin flippers, a
rolling ball, a six-legged walker, a full-body spinner, axes, ram spikes,

- **Parts:** box, wedge, flat plate, bar, cylinder/disc, cone, sphere, capsule,
  or a custom convex hull from your own points. Each one has a material
  (aluminium, mild steel, hardened steel, titanium, HDPE, polycarbonate,
  rubber, PTFE, plywood) and is either solid or a hollow shell with a wall
  thickness. Its size, position, rotation and shape offset are all editable.

  steering, weapon buttons 1–4 (held or toggled), or the walking gait

p## The Garage

Robots are **trees of parts joined by joints**, so you can build almost
anything that's rigid bits, hinges, sliders and motors: twin flippers, a
rolling ball, a six-legged walker, a full-body spinner, axes, ram spikes,
lifters, clampers…

- **Parts:** box, wedge, flat plate, bar, cylinder/disc, cone, sphere, capsule,
  or a custom convex hull from your own points. Each one has a material
  (aluminium, mild steel, hardened steel, titanium, HDPE, polycarbonate,
  rubber, PTFE, plywood) and is either solid or a hollow shell with a wall
  thickness. Its size, position, rotation and shape offset are all editable.
- **Joints:** every part is *fixed* to its parent, on a *hinge* (with an axis and
  optional angle limits), or on a *slider* (with travel limits).
- **Actuators** on any hinge or slider:
  - a **DC motor** through a gearbox, for wheels, spinners and drums;
  - a **pneumatic ram**, with your choice of ram, valve and pressure, for
    flippers, lifters, axes and spikes;
  - a **servo**, which holds positions, for legs, clamps and steering.
- **Wiring:** any actuator can follow the left or right drive, throttle,
  steering, weapon buttons 1–4 (held or toggled), or the walking gait
  (stride side, phase, swing or lift).
- **Internals:** batteries (in parallel), gas bottles (one shared supply) and
  ballast.
- **Tools:** add from a parts menu (including ready-wired assemblies such as a
  leg with hip and knee servos, an axe, a spinner or a ram spike), mirror a
  part with everything on it to the other side, duplicate, move it onto
  another part, or remove it. Click a part in the 3D view to select it.

Stats update as you build: weight, cost, drive (top speed and pushing force
for wheeled robots), battery life, and each weapon's force or stored energy
and spin-up time. There's also a full parts list with spares and rebuild time.
**Scrutineering** checks weight class, budget, size, parts below the floor,
voltage against each motor, gas for the pneumatics, wiring and battery life.
The **test bay** behind the editor lets you drive the robot against a
crash-test dummy, with live telemetry for every joint.

Starter robots: Wedgehog (wedge), Flipside (flipper), Whirlwind (undercutter),
Twin Terror (two flippers), Orb (pendulum-drive sphere), Arachnid (six-legged
walker) and Gyrodisc (full-body spinner). Saved robots appear on the fight
select screen. Designs are plain JSON, so you can copy one out to share it or
paste one in; old saves are upgraded automatically.

- **Parts:** box, wedge, flat plate, bar, cylinder/disc, cone, sphere, capsule,
  or a custom convex hull from your own points. Each one has a material
  (aluminium, mild steel, hardened steel, titanium, HDPE, polycarbonate,
  rubber, PTFE, plywood) and is either solid or a hollow shell with a wall
  thickness. Its size, position, rotation and shape offset are all editable.

  optional angle limits), or on a *slider* (with travel limits).
- **Actuators** on any hinge or slider:
  - a **DC motor** through a gearbox, for wheels, spinners and drums;
  - a **pneumatic ram**, with your choice of ram, valve and pressure, for
    flippers, lifters, axes and spikes;
  - a **servo**, which holds positions, for legs, clamps and steering.
- **Wiring:** any actuator can follow the left or right drive, throttle,
  steering, weapon buttons 1–4 (held or toggled), or the walking gait
  (stride side, phase, swing or lift).
- **Internals:** batteries (in parallel), gas bottles (one shared supply) and
  ballast.

and spin-up time. There's also a full parts list with spares and rebuild time.
**Scrutineering** checks weight class, budget, size, parts below the floor,
voltage against each motor, gas for the pneumatics, wiring and battery life.
The **test bay** behind the editor lets you drive the robot against a
crash-test dummy, with live telemetry for every joint.

Starter robots: Wedgehog (wedge), Flipside (flipper), Whirlwind (undercutter),
Twin Terror (two flippers), Orb (pendulum-drive sphere), Arachnid (six-legged
walker) and Gyrodisc (full-body spinner). Saved robots appear on the fight
select screen. Designs are plain JSON, so you can copy one out to share it or
paste one in; old saves are upgraded automatically.

 ## The Garage

Robots are **trees of parts joined by joints**, so you can build almost
anything that's rigid bits, hinges, sliders and motors: twin flippers, a
rolling ball, a six-legged walker, a full-body spinner, axes, ram spikes,
lifters, clampers…

- **Parts:** box, wedge, flat plate, bar, cylinder/disc, cone, sphere, capsule,
  or a custom convex hull from your own points. Each one has a material
  (aluminium, mild steel, hardened steel, titanium, HDPE, polycarbonate,
  rubber, PTFE, plywood) and is either solid or a hollow shell with a wall
  thickness. Its size, position, rotation and shape offset are all editable.
- **Joints:** every part is *fixed* to its parent, on a *hinge* (with an axis and
  optional angle limits), or on a *slider* (with travel limits).
- **Actuators** on any hinge or slider:
  - a **DC motor** through a gearbox, for wheels, spinners and drums;
  - a **pneumatic ram**, with your choice of ram, valve and pressure, for
    flippers, lifters, axes and spikes;
  - a **servo**, which holds positions, for legs, clamps and steering.
- **Wiring:** any actuator can follow the left or right drive, throttle,
  steering, weapon buttons 1–4 (held or toggled), or the walking gait
  (stride side, phase, swing or lift).
- **Internals:** batteries (in parallel), gas bottles (one shared supply) and
  ballast.
- **Tools:** add from a parts menu (including ready-wired assemblies such as a
  leg with hip and knee servos, an axe, a spinner or a ram spike), mirror a
  part with everything on it to the other side, duplicate, move it onto
  another part, or remove it. Click a part in the 3D view to select it.

Stats update as you build: weight, cost, drive (top speed and pushing force
for wheeled robots), battery life, and each weapon's force or stored energy
and spin-up time. There's also a full parts list with spares and rebuild time.
**Scrutineering** checks weight class, budget, size, parts below the floor,
voltage against each motor, gas for the pneumatics, wiring and battery life.
The **test bay** behind the editor lets you drive the robot against a
crash-test dummy, with live telemetry for every joint.

l## The Garage

Robots are **trees of parts joined by joints**, so you can build almost
anything that's rigid bits, hinges, sliders and motors: twin flippers, a
rolling ball, a six-legged walker, a full-body spinner, axes, ram spikes,
lifters, clampers…

- **Parts:** box, wedge, flat plate, bar, cylinder/disc, cone, sphere, capsule,
  or a custom convex hull from your own points. Each one has a material
  (aluminium, mild steel, hardened steel, titanium, HDPE, polycarbonate,
  rubber, PTFE, plywood) and is either solid or a hollow shell with a wall
  thickness. Its size, position, rotation and shape offset are all editable.
- **Joints:** every part is *fixed* to its parent, on a *hinge* (with an axis and
  optional angle limits), or on a *slider* (with travel limits).
- **Actuators** on any hinge or slider:
  - a **DC motor** through a gearbox, for wheels, spinners and drums;
  - a **pneumatic ram**, with your choice of ram, valve and pressure, for
    flippers, lifters, axes and spikes;
  - a **servo**, which holds positions, for legs, clamps and steering.
- **Wiring:** any actuator can follow the left or right drive, throttle,
  steering, weapon buttons 1–4 (held or toggled), or the walking gait
  (stride side, phase, swing or lift).
- **Internals:** batteries (in parallel), gas bottles (one shared supply) and
  ballast.
- **Tools:** add from a parts menu (including ready-wired assemblies such as a
  leg with hip and knee servos, an axe, a spinner or a ram spike), mirror a
  part with everything on it to the other side, duplicate, move it onto
  another part, or remove it. Click a part in the 3D view to select it.

Stats update as you build: weight, cost, drive (top speed and pushing force

e## The Garage

Robots are **trees of parts joined by joints**, so you can build almost
anything that's rigid bits, hinges, sliders and motors: twin flippers, a
rolling ball, a six-legged walker, a full-body spinner, axes, ram spikes,
lifters, clampers…

- **Parts:** box, wedge, flat plate, bar, cylinder/disc, cone, sphere, capsule,
  or a custom convex hull from your own points. Each one has a material
  (aluminium, mild steel, hardened steel, titanium, HDPE, polycarbonate,
  rubber, PTFE, plywood) and is either solid or a hollow shell with a wall
  thickness. Its size, position, rotation and shape offset are all editable.
- **Joints:** every part is *fixed* to its parent, on a *hinge* (with an axis and
  optional angle limits), or on a *slider* (with travel limits).
- **Actuators** on any hinge or slider:
  - a **DC motor** through a gearbox, for wheels, spinners and drums;
  - a **pneumatic ram**, with your choice of ram, valve and pressure, for
    flippers, lifters, axes and spikes;
  - a **servo**, which holds positions, for legs, clamps and steering.
- **Wiring:** any actuator can follow the left or right drive, throttle,
  steering, weapon buttons 1–4 (held or toggled), or the walking gait
  (stride side, phase, swing or lift).
- **Internals:** batteries (in parallel), gas bottles (one shared supply) and
  ballast.
- **Tools:** add from a parts menu (including ready-wired assemblies such as a
  leg with hip and knee servos, an axe, a spinner or a ram spike), mirror a
  part with everything on it to the other side, duplicate, move it onto
  another part, or remove it. Click a part in the 3D view to select it.

Stats update as you build: weight, cost, drive (top speed and pushing force
for wheeled robots), battery life, and each weapon's force or stored energy
and spin-up time. There's also a full parts list with spares and rebuild time.
**Scrutineering** checks weight class, budget, size, parts below the floor,
voltage against each motor, gas for the pneumatics, wiring and battery life.
The **test bay** behind the editor lets you drive the robot against a
crash-test dummy, with live telemetry for every joint.

Starter robots: Wedgehog (wedge), Flipside (flipper), Whirlwind (undercutter),
Twin Terror (two flippers), Orb (pendulum-drive sphere), Arachnid (six-legged
walker) and Gyrodisc (full-body spinner). Saved robots appear on the fight
select screen. Designs are plain JSON, so you can copy one out to share it or
paste one in; old saves are upgraded automatically.

- **Parts:** box, wedge, flat plate, bar, cylinder/disc, cone, sphere, capsule,
  or a custom convex hull from your own points. Each one has a material
  (aluminium, mild steel, hardened steel, titanium, HDPE, polycarbonate,
  rubber, PTFE, plywood) and is either solid or a hollow shell with a wall
  thickness. Its size, position, rotation and shape offset are all editable.
- **Joints:** every part is *fixed* to its parent, on a *hinge* (with an axis and
  optional angle limits), or on a *slider* (with travel limits).
- **Actuators** on any hinge or slider:
  - a **DC motor** through a gearbox, for wheels, spinners and drums;
  - a **pneumatic ram**, with your choice of ram, valve and pressure, for
    flippers, lifters, axes and spikes;
  - a **servo**, which holds positions, for legs, clamps and steering.
- **Wiring:** any actuator can follow the left or right drive, throttle,
  steering, weapon buttons 1–4 (held or toggled), or the walking gait
  (stride side, phase, swing or lift).
- **Internals:** batteries (in parallel), gas bottles (one shared supply) and
  ballast.
- **Tools:** add from a parts menu (including ready-wired assemblies such as a
  leg with hip and knee servos, an axe, a spinner or a ram spike), mirror a
  part with everything on it to the other side, duplicate, move it onto
  another part, or remove it. Click a part in the 3D view to select it.

Stats update as you build: weight, cost, drive (top speed and pushing force
for wheeled robots), battery life, and each weapon's force or stored energy
and spin-up time. There's also a full parts list with spares and rebuild time.
**Scrutineering** checks weight class, budget, size, parts below the floor,
voltage against each motor, gas for the pneumatics, wiring and battery life.

and spin-up time. There's also a full parts list with spares and rebuild time.
**Scrutineering** checks weight class, budget, size, parts below the floor,
voltage against each motor, gas for the pneumatics, wiring and battery life.
The **test bay** behind the editor lets you drive the robot against a
crash-test dummy, with live telemetry for every joint.

Starter robots: Wedgehog (wedge), Flipside (flipper), Whirlwind (undercutter),
Twin Terror (two flippers), Orb (pendulum-drive sphere), Arachnid (six-legged
walker) and Gyrodisc (full-body spinner). Saved robots appear on the fight
select screen. Designs are plain JSON, so you can copy one out to share it or
paste one in; old saves are upgraded automatically.

,## The Garage

Robots are **trees of parts joined by joints**, so you can build almost
anything that's rigid bits, hinges, sliders and motors: twin flippers, a
rolling ball, a six-legged walker, a full-body spinner, axes, ram spikes,
lifters, clampers…

- **Parts:** box, wedge, flat plate, bar, cylinder/disc, cone, sphere, capsule,
  or a custom convex hull from your own points. Each one has a material
  (aluminium, mild steel, hardened steel, titanium, HDPE, polycarbonate,
  rubber, PTFE, plywood) and is either solid or a hollow shell with a wall
  thickness. Its size, position, rotation and shape offset are all editable.
- **Joints:** every part is *fixed* to its parent, on a *hinge* (with an axis and
  optional angle limits), or on a *slider* (with travel limits).
- **Actuators** on any hinge or slider:
  - a **DC motor** through a gearbox, for wheels, spinners and drums;
  - a **pneumatic ram**, with your choice of ram, valve and pressure, for
    flippers, lifters, axes and spikes;
  - a **servo**, which holds positions, for legs, clamps and steering.
- **Wiring:** any actuator can follow the left or right drive, throttle,
  steering, weapon buttons 1–4 (held or toggled), or the walking gait
  (stride side, phase, swing or lift).
- **Internals:** batteries (in parallel), gas bottles (one shared supply) and
  ballast.
- **Tools:** add from a parts menu (including ready-wired assemblies such as a
  leg with hip and knee servos, an axe, a spinner or a ram spike), mirror a
  part with everything on it to the other side, duplicate, move it onto
  another part, or remove it. Click a part in the 3D view to select it.

Stats update as you build: weight, cost, drive (top speed and pushing force
for wheeled robots), battery life, and each weapon's force or stored energy
and spin-up time. There's also a full parts list with spares and rebuild time.
**Scrutineering** checks weight class, budget, size, parts below the floor,
voltage against each motor, gas for the pneumatics, wiring and battery life.

t## The Garage

Robots are **trees of parts joined by joints**, so you can build almost
anything that's rigid bits, hinges, sliders and motors: twin flippers, a
rolling ball, a six-legged walker, a full-body spinner, axes, ram spikes,
lifters, clampers…

- **Parts:** box, wedge, flat plate, bar, cylinder/disc, cone, sphere, capsule,
  or a custom convex hull from your own points. Each one has a material
  (aluminium, mild steel, hardened steel, titanium, HDPE, polycarbonate,
  rubber, PTFE, plywood) and is either solid or a hollow shell with a wall
  thickness. Its size, position, rotation and shape offset are all editable.
- **Joints:** every part is *fixed* to its parent, on a *hinge* (with an axis and
  optional angle limits), or on a *slider* (with travel limits).
- **Actuators** on any hinge or slider:
  - a **DC motor** through a gearbox, for wheels, spinners and drums;
  - a **pneumatic ram**, with your choice of ram, valve and pressure, for
    flippers, lifters, axes and spikes;
  - a **servo**, which holds positions, for legs, clamps and steering.
- **Wiring:** any actuator can follow the left or right drive, throttle,
  steering, weapon buttons 1–4 (held or toggled), or the walking gait
  (stride side, phase, swing or lift).
- **Internals:** batteries (in parallel), gas bottles (one shared supply) and
  ballast.
- **Tools:** add from a parts menu (including ready-wired assemblies such as a
  leg with hip and knee servos, an axe, a spinner or a ram spike), mirror a
  part with everything on it to the other side, duplicate, move it onto
  another part, or remove it. Click a part in the 3D view to select it.

Stats update as you build: weight, cost, drive (top speed and pushing force
for wheeled robots), battery life, and each weapon's force or stored energy
and spin-up time. There's also a full parts list with spares and rebuild time.
**Scrutineering** checks weight class, budget, size, parts below the floor,

a## The Garage

Robots are **trees of parts joined by joints**, so you can build almost
anything that's rigid bits, hinges, sliders and motors: twin flippers, a
rolling ball, a six-legged walker, a full-body spinner, axes, ram spikes,
lifters, clampers…

- **Parts:** box, wedge, flat plate, bar, cylinder/disc, cone, sphere, capsule,
  or a custom convex hull from your own points. Each one has a material
  (aluminium, mild steel, hardened steel, titanium, HDPE, polycarbonate,
  rubber, PTFE, plywood) and is either solid or a hollow shell with a wall
  thickness. Its size, position, rotation and shape offset are all editable.
- **Joints:** every part is *fixed* to its parent, on a *hinge* (with an axis and
  optional angle limits), or on a *slider* (with travel limits).
- **Actuators** on any hinge or slider:
  - a **DC motor** through a gearbox, for wheels, spinners and drums;
  - a **pneumatic ram**, with your choice of ram, valve and pressure, for
    flippers, lifters, axes and spikes;
  - a **servo**, which holds positions, for legs, clamps and steering.
- **Wiring:** any actuator can follow the left or right drive, throttle,
  steering, weapon buttons 1–4 (held or toggled), or the walking gait
  (stride side, phase, swing or lift).
- **Internals:** batteries (in parallel), gas bottles (one shared supply) and
  ballast.
- **Tools:** add from a parts menu (including ready-wired assemblies such as a
  leg with hip and knee servos, an axe, a spinner or a ram spike), mirror a
  part with everything on it to the other side, duplicate, move it onto
  another part, or remove it. Click a part in the 3D view to select it.

Stats update as you build: weight, cost, drive (top speed and pushing force
for wheeled robots), battery life, and each weapon's force or stored energy
and spin-up time. There's also a full parts list with spares and rebuild time.
**Scrutineering** checks weight class, budget, size, parts below the floor,
voltage against each motor, gas for the pneumatics, wiring and battery life.
The **test bay** behind the editor lets you drive the robot against a
crash-test dummy, with live telemetry for every joint.

Starter robots: Wedgehog (wedge), Flipside (flipper), Whirlwind (undercutter),
Twin Terror (two flippers), Orb (pendulum-drive sphere), Arachnid (six-legged
walker) and Gyrodisc (full-body spinner). Saved robots appear on the fight
select screen. Designs are plain JSON, so you can copy one out to share it or
paste one in; old saves are upgraded automatically.

- **Parts:** box, wedge, flat plate, bar, cylinder/disc, cone, sphere, capsule,
  or a custom convex hull from your own points. Each one has a material
  (aluminium, mild steel, hardened steel, titanium, HDPE, polycarbonate,
  rubber, PTFE, plywood) and is either solid or a hollow shell with a wall
  thickness. Its size, position, rotation and shape offset are all editable.
- **Joints:** every part is *fixed* to its parent, on a *hinge* (with an axis and
  optional angle limits), or on a *slider* (with travel limits).
- **Actuators** on any hinge or slider:
  - a **DC motor** through a gearbox, for wheels, spinners and drums;
  - a **pneumatic ram**, with your choice of ram, valve and pressure, for
    flippers, lifters, axes and spikes;
  - a **servo**, which holds positions, for legs, clamps and steering.
- **Wiring:** any actuator can follow the left or right drive, throttle,
  steering, weapon buttons 1–4 (held or toggled), or the walking gait
  (stride side, phase, swing or lift).
- **Internals:** batteries (in parallel), gas bottles (one shared supply) and
  ballast.
- **Tools:** add from a parts menu (including ready-wired assemblies such as a
  leg with hip and knee servos, an axe, a spinner or a ram spike), mirror a
  part with everything on it to the other side, duplicate, move it onto
  another part, or remove it. Click a part in the 3D view to select it.

Stats update as you build: weight, cost, drive (top speed and pushing force
for wheeled robots), battery life, and each weapon's force or stored energy
and spin-up time. There's also a full parts list with spares and rebuild time.
**Scrutineering** checks weight class, budget, size, parts below the floor,
voltage against each motor, gas for the pneumatics, wiring and battery life.

and spin-up time. There's also a full parts list with spares and rebuild time.

Starter robots: Wedgehog (wedge), Flipside (flipper), Whirlwind (undercutter),

r## The Garage

Robots are **trees of parts joined by joints**, so you can build almost
anything that's rigid bits, hinges, sliders and motors: twin flippers, a
rolling ball, a six-legged walker, a full-body spinner, axes, ram spikes,
lifters, clampers…

- **Parts:** box, wedge, flat plate, bar, cylinder/disc, cone, sphere, capsule,
  or a custom convex hull from your own points. Each one has a material
  (aluminium, mild steel, hardened steel, titanium, HDPE, polycarbonate,
  rubber, PTFE, plywood) and is either solid or a hollow shell with a wall
  thickness. Its size, position, rotation and shape offset are all editable.
- **Joints:** every part is *fixed* to its parent, on a *hinge* (with an axis and
  optional angle limits), or on a *slider* (with travel limits).
- **Actuators** on any hinge or slider:
  - a **DC motor** through a gearbox, for wheels, spinners and drums;
  - a **pneumatic ram**, with your choice of ram, valve and pressure, for
    flippers, lifters, axes and spikes;
  - a **servo**, which holds positions, for legs, clamps and steering.
- **Wiring:** any actuator can follow the left or right drive, throttle,
  steering, weapon buttons 1–4 (held or toggled), or the walking gait
  (stride side, phase, swing or lift).
- **Internals:** batteries (in parallel), gas bottles (one shared supply) and
  ballast.
- **Tools:** add from a parts menu (including ready-wired assemblies such as a
  leg with hip and knee servos, an axe, a spinner or a ram spike), mirror a
  part with everything on it to the other side, duplicate, move it onto
  another part, or remove it. Click a part in the 3D view to select it.

Stats update as you build: weight, cost, drive (top speed and pushing force
for wheeled robots), battery life, and each weapon's force or stored energy
and spin-up time. There's also a full parts list with spares and rebuild time.
**Scrutineering** checks weight class, budget, size, parts below the floor,

b## The Garage

Robots are **trees of parts joined by joints**, so you can build almost
anything that's rigid bits, hinges, sliders and motors: twin flippers, a
rolling ball, a six-legged walker, a full-body spinner, axes, ram spikes,
lifters, clampers…

- **Parts:** box, wedge, flat plate, bar, cylinder/disc, cone, sphere, capsule,
  or a custom convex hull from your own points. Each one has a material
  (aluminium, mild steel, hardened steel, titanium, HDPE, polycarbonate,
  rubber, PTFE, plywood) and is either solid or a hollow shell with a wall
  thickness. Its size, position, rotation and shape offset are all editable.
- **Joints:** every part is *fixed* to its parent, on a *hinge* (with an axis and
  optional angle limits), or on a *slider* (with travel limits).
- **Actuators** on any hinge or slider:
  - a **DC motor** through a gearbox, for wheels, spinners and drums;
  - a **pneumatic ram**, with your choice of ram, valve and pressure, for
    flippers, lifters, axes and spikes;
  - a **servo**, which holds positions, for legs, clamps and steering.
- **Wiring:** any actuator can follow the left or right drive, throttle,
  steering, weapon buttons 1–4 (held or toggled), or the walking gait
  (stride side, phase, swing or lift).
- **Internals:** batteries (in parallel), gas bottles (one shared supply) and
  ballast.
- **Tools:** add from a parts menu (including ready-wired assemblies such as a
  leg with hip and knee servos, an axe, a spinner or a ram spike), mirror a
  part with everything on it to the other side, duplicate, move it onto
  another part, or remove it. Click a part in the 3D view to select it.

Stats update as you build: weight, cost, drive (top speed and pushing force
for wheeled robots), battery life, and each weapon's force or stored energy
and spin-up time. There's also a full parts list with spares and rebuild time.
**Scrutineering** checks weight class, budget, size, parts below the floor,
voltage against each motor, gas for the pneumatics, wiring and battery life.

 ## The Garage

Robots are **trees of parts joined by joints**, so you can build almost
anything that's rigid bits, hinges, sliders and motors: twin flippers, a
rolling ball, a six-legged walker, a full-body spinner, axes, ram spikes,
lifters, clampers…

- **Parts:** box, wedge, flat plate, bar, cylinder/disc, cone, sphere, capsule,
  or a custom convex hull from your own points. Each one has a material
  (aluminium, mild steel, hardened steel, titanium, HDPE, polycarbonate,
  rubber, PTFE, plywood) and is either solid or a hollow shell with a wall
  thickness. Its size, position, rotation and shape offset are all editable.
- **Joints:** every part is *fixed* to its parent, on a *hinge* (with an axis and
  optional angle limits), or on a *slider* (with travel limits).
- **Actuators** on any hinge or slider:
  - a **DC motor** through a gearbox, for wheels, spinners and drums;
  - a **pneumatic ram**, with your choice of ram, valve and pressure, for
    flippers, lifters, axes and spikes;
  - a **servo**, which holds positions, for legs, clamps and steering.
- **Wiring:** any actuator can follow the left or right drive, throttle,
  steering, weapon buttons 1–4 (held or toggled), or the walking gait
  (stride side, phase, swing or lift).
- **Internals:** batteries (in parallel), gas bottles (one shared supply) and
  ballast.
- **Tools:** add from a parts menu (including ready-wired assemblies such as a
  leg with hip and knee servos, an axe, a spinner or a ram spike), mirror a
  part with everything on it to the other side, duplicate, move it onto
  another part, or remove it. Click a part in the 3D view to select it.

Stats update as you build: weight, cost, drive (top speed and pushing force
for wheeled robots), battery life, and each weapon's force or stored energy
and spin-up time. There's also a full parts list with spares and rebuild time.
**Scrutineering** checks weight class, budget, size, parts below the floor,
voltage against each motor, gas for the pneumatics, wiring and battery life.
The **test bay** behind the editor lets you drive the robot against a
crash-test dummy, with live telemetry for every joint.

Starter robots: Wedgehog (wedge), Flipside (flipper), Whirlwind (undercutter),
Twin Terror (two flippers), Orb (pendulum-drive sphere), Arachnid (six-legged
walker) and Gyrodisc (full-body spinner). Saved robots appear on the fight
select screen. Designs are plain JSON, so you can copy one out to share it or
paste one in; old saves are upgraded automatically.

- **Parts:** box, wedge, flat plate, bar, cylinder/disc, cone, sphere, capsule,
  or a custom convex hull from your own points. Each one has a material
  (aluminium, mild steel, hardened steel, titanium, HDPE, polycarbonate,
  rubber, PTFE, plywood) and is either solid or a hollow shell with a wall
  thickness. Its size, position, rotation and shape offset are all editable.
- **Joints:** every part is *fixed* to its parent, on a *hinge* (with an axis and
  optional angle limits), or on a *slider* (with travel limits).
- **Actuators** on any hinge or slider:
  - a **DC motor** through a gearbox, for wheels, spinners and drums;
  - a **pneumatic ram**, with your choice of ram, valve and pressure, for
    flippers, lifters, axes and spikes;
  - a **servo**, which holds positions, for legs, clamps and steering.
- **Wiring:** any actuator can follow the left or right drive, throttle,
  steering, weapon buttons 1–4 (held or toggled), or the walking gait
  (stride side, phase, swing or lift).
- **Internals:** batteries (in parallel), gas bottles (one shared supply) and
  ballast.

  leg with hip and knee servos, an axe, a spinner or a ram spike), mirror a

Stats update as you build: weight, cost, drive (top speed and pushing force

e## The Garage

Robots are **trees of parts joined by joints**, so you can build almost
anything that's rigid bits, hinges, sliders and motors: twin flippers, a
rolling ball, a six-legged walker, a full-body spinner, axes, ram spikes,
lifters, clampers…

- **Parts:** box, wedge, flat plate, bar, cylinder/disc, cone, sphere, capsule,
  or a custom convex hull from your own points. Each one has a material
  (aluminium, mild steel, hardened steel, titanium, HDPE, polycarbonate,
  rubber, PTFE, plywood) and is either solid or a hollow shell with a wall
  thickness. Its size, position, rotation and shape offset are all editable.
- **Joints:** every part is *fixed* to its parent, on a *hinge* (with an axis and
  optional angle limits), or on a *slider* (with travel limits).
- **Actuators** on any hinge or slider:
  - a **DC motor** through a gearbox, for wheels, spinners and drums;
  - a **pneumatic ram**, with your choice of ram, valve and pressure, for
    flippers, lifters, axes and spikes;
  - a **servo**, which holds positions, for legs, clamps and steering.
- **Wiring:** any actuator can follow the left or right drive, throttle,
  steering, weapon buttons 1–4 (held or toggled), or the walking gait
  (stride side, phase, swing or lift).
- **Internals:** batteries (in parallel), gas bottles (one shared supply) and
  ballast.
- **Tools:** add from a parts menu (including ready-wired assemblies such as a
  leg with hip and knee servos, an axe, a spinner or a ram spike), mirror a
  part with everything on it to the other side, duplicate, move it onto
  another part, or remove it. Click a part in the 3D view to select it.

,## The Garage

Robots are **trees of parts joined by joints**, so you can build almost
anything that's rigid bits, hinges, sliders and motors: twin flippers, a
rolling ball, a six-legged walker, a full-body spinner, axes, ram spikes,
lifters, clampers…

- **Parts:** box, wedge, flat plate, bar, cylinder/disc, cone, sphere, capsule,
  or a custom convex hull from your own points. Each one has a material
  (aluminium, mild steel, hardened steel, titanium, HDPE, polycarbonate,
  rubber, PTFE, plywood) and is either solid or a hollow shell with a wall
  thickness. Its size, position, rotation and shape offset are all editable.
- **Joints:** every part is *fixed* to its parent, on a *hinge* (with an axis and
  optional angle limits), or on a *slider* (with travel limits).
- **Actuators** on any hinge or slider:
  - a **DC motor** through a gearbox, for wheels, spinners and drums;
  - a **pneumatic ram**, with your choice of ram, valve and pressure, for
    flippers, lifters, axes and spikes;
  - a **servo**, which holds positions, for legs, clamps and steering.
- **Wiring:** any actuator can follow the left or right drive, throttle,
  steering, weapon buttons 1–4 (held or toggled), or the walking gait
  (stride side, phase, swing or lift).
- **Internals:** batteries (in parallel), gas bottles (one shared supply) and
  ballast.
- **Tools:** add from a parts menu (including ready-wired assemblies such as a
  leg with hip and knee servos, an axe, a spinner or a ram spike), mirror a
  part with everything on it to the other side, duplicate, move it onto
  another part, or remove it. Click a part in the 3D view to select it.

Stats update as you build: weight, cost, drive (top speed and pushing force
for wheeled robots), battery life, and each weapon's force or stored energy
and spin-up time. There's also a full parts list with spares and rebuild time.
**Scrutineering** checks weight class, budget, size, parts below the floor,

 ## The Garage

Robots are **trees of parts joined by joints**, so you can build almost
anything that's rigid bits, hinges, sliders and motors: twin flippers, a
rolling ball, a six-legged walker, a full-body spinner, axes, ram spikes,
lifters, clampers…

- **Parts:** box, wedge, flat plate, bar, cylinder/disc, cone, sphere, capsule,
  or a custom convex hull from your own points. Each one has a material
  (aluminium, mild steel, hardened steel, titanium, HDPE, polycarbonate,
  rubber, PTFE, plywood) and is either solid or a hollow shell with a wall
  thickness. Its size, position, rotation and shape offset are all editable.
- **Joints:** every part is *fixed* to its parent, on a *hinge* (with an axis and
  optional angle limits), or on a *slider* (with travel limits).
- **Actuators** on any hinge or slider:
  - a **DC motor** through a gearbox, for wheels, spinners and drums;
  - a **pneumatic ram**, with your choice of ram, valve and pressure, for
    flippers, lifters, axes and spikes;
  - a **servo**, which holds positions, for legs, clamps and steering.
- **Wiring:** any actuator can follow the left or right drive, throttle,
  steering, weapon buttons 1–4 (held or toggled), or the walking gait
  (stride side, phase, swing or lift).
- **Internals:** batteries (in parallel), gas bottles (one shared supply) and
  ballast.
- **Tools:** add from a parts menu (including ready-wired assemblies such as a
  leg with hip and knee servos, an axe, a spinner or a ram spike), mirror a
  part with everything on it to the other side, duplicate, move it onto
  another part, or remove it. Click a part in the 3D view to select it.

Stats update as you build: weight, cost, drive (top speed and pushing force
for wheeled robots), battery life, and each weapon's force or stored energy
and spin-up time. There's also a full parts list with spares and rebuild time.
**Scrutineering** checks weight class, budget, size, parts below the floor,
voltage against each motor, gas for the pneumatics, wiring and battery life.
The **test bay** behind the editor lets you drive the robot against a
crash-test dummy, with live telemetry for every joint.

Starter robots: Wedgehog (wedge), Flipside (flipper), Whirlwind (undercutter),
Twin Terror (two flippers), Orb (pendulum-drive sphere), Arachnid (six-legged
walker) and Gyrodisc (full-body spinner). Saved robots appear on the fight
select screen. Designs are plain JSON, so you can copy one out to share it or
paste one in; old saves are upgraded automatically.

- **Parts:** box, wedge, flat plate, bar, cylinder/disc, cone, sphere, capsule,
  or a custom convex hull from your own points. Each one has a material
  (aluminium, mild steel, hardened steel, titanium, HDPE, polycarbonate,
  rubber, PTFE, plywood) and is either solid or a hollow shell with a wall
  thickness. Its size, position, rotation and shape offset are all editable.
- **Joints:** every part is *fixed* to its parent, on a *hinge* (with an axis and
  optional angle limits), or on a *slider* (with travel limits).
- **Actuators** on any hinge or slider:
  - a **DC motor** through a gearbox, for wheels, spinners and drums;
  - a **pneumatic ram**, with your choice of ram, valve and pressure, for
    flippers, lifters, axes and spikes;
  - a **servo**, which holds positions, for legs, clamps and steering.
- **Wiring:** any actuator can follow the left or right drive, throttle,
  steering, weapon buttons 1–4 (held or toggled), or the walking gait
  (stride side, phase, swing or lift).
- **Internals:** batteries (in parallel), gas bottles (one shared supply) and
  ballast.
- **Tools:** add from a parts menu (including ready-wired assemblies such as a
  leg with hip and knee servos, an axe, a spinner or a ram spike), mirror a
  part with everything on it to the other side, duplicate, move it onto
  another part, or remove it. Click a part in the 3D view to select it.

Stats update as you build: weight, cost, drive (top speed and pushing force
for wheeled robots), battery life, and each weapon's force or stored energy
and spin-up time. There's also a full parts list with spares and rebuild time.
**Scrutineering** checks weight class, budget, size, parts below the floor,
voltage against each motor, gas for the pneumatics, wiring and battery life.
The **test bay** behind the editor lets you drive the robot against a
crash-test dummy, with live telemetry for every joint.

Starter robots: Wedgehog (wedge), Flipside (flipper), Whirlwind (undercutter),

walker) and Gyrodisc (full-body spinner). Saved robots appear on the fight

o## The Garage

Robots are **trees of parts joined by joints**, so you can build almost
anything that's rigid bits, hinges, sliders and motors: twin flippers, a
rolling ball, a six-legged walker, a full-body spinner, axes, ram spikes,
lifters, clampers…

- **Parts:** box, wedge, flat plate, bar, cylinder/disc, cone, sphere, capsule,
  or a custom convex hull from your own points. Each one has a material
  (aluminium, mild steel, hardened steel, titanium, HDPE, polycarbonate,
  rubber, PTFE, plywood) and is either solid or a hollow shell with a wall
  thickness. Its size, position, rotation and shape offset are all editable.
- **Joints:** every part is *fixed* to its parent, on a *hinge* (with an axis and
  optional angle limits), or on a *slider* (with travel limits).
- **Actuators** on any hinge or slider:
  - a **DC motor** through a gearbox, for wheels, spinners and drums;
  - a **pneumatic ram**, with your choice of ram, valve and pressure, for
    flippers, lifters, axes and spikes;
  - a **servo**, which holds positions, for legs, clamps and steering.
- **Wiring:** any actuator can follow the left or right drive, throttle,
  steering, weapon buttons 1–4 (held or toggled), or the walking gait
  (stride side, phase, swing or lift).
- **Internals:** batteries (in parallel), gas bottles (one shared supply) and
  ballast.
- **Tools:** add from a parts menu (including ready-wired assemblies such as a
  leg with hip and knee servos, an axe, a spinner or a ram spike), mirror a
  part with everything on it to the other side, duplicate, move it onto
  another part, or remove it. Click a part in the 3D view to select it.

r## The Garage

Robots are **trees of parts joined by joints**, so you can build almost
anything that's rigid bits, hinges, sliders and motors: twin flippers, a
rolling ball, a six-legged walker, a full-body spinner, axes, ram spikes,
lifters, clampers…

- **Parts:** box, wedge, flat plate, bar, cylinder/disc, cone, sphere, capsule,
  or a custom convex hull from your own points. Each one has a material
  (aluminium, mild steel, hardened steel, titanium, HDPE, polycarbonate,
  rubber, PTFE, plywood) and is either solid or a hollow shell with a wall
  thickness. Its size, position, rotation and shape offset are all editable.
- **Joints:** every part is *fixed* to its parent, on a *hinge* (with an axis and
  optional angle limits), or on a *slider* (with travel limits).
- **Actuators** on any hinge or slider:
  - a **DC motor** through a gearbox, for wheels, spinners and drums;
  - a **pneumatic ram**, with your choice of ram, valve and pressure, for
    flippers, lifters, axes and spikes;
  - a **servo**, which holds positions, for legs, clamps and steering.
- **Wiring:** any actuator can follow the left or right drive, throttle,
  steering, weapon buttons 1–4 (held or toggled), or the walking gait
  (stride side, phase, swing or lift).
- **Internals:** batteries (in parallel), gas bottles (one shared supply) and
  ballast.
- **Tools:** add from a parts menu (including ready-wired assemblies such as a
  leg with hip and knee servos, an axe, a spinner or a ram spike), mirror a
  part with everything on it to the other side, duplicate, move it onto
  another part, or remove it. Click a part in the 3D view to select it.

Stats update as you build: weight, cost, drive (top speed and pushing force
for wheeled robots), battery life, and each weapon's force or stored energy
and spin-up time. There's also a full parts list with spares and rebuild time.
**Scrutineering** checks weight class, budget, size, parts below the floor,

g## The Garage

Robots are **trees of parts joined by joints**, so you can build almost
anything that's rigid bits, hinges, sliders and motors: twin flippers, a
rolling ball, a six-legged walker, a full-body spinner, axes, ram spikes,
lifters, clampers…

- **Parts:** box, wedge, flat plate, bar, cylinder/disc, cone, sphere, capsule,
  or a custom convex hull from your own points. Each one has a material
  (aluminium, mild steel, hardened steel, titanium, HDPE, polycarbonate,
  rubber, PTFE, plywood) and is either solid or a hollow shell with a wall
  thickness. Its size, position, rotation and shape offset are all editable.
- **Joints:** every part is *fixed* to its parent, on a *hinge* (with an axis and
  optional angle limits), or on a *slider* (with travel limits).
- **Actuators** on any hinge or slider:
  - a **DC motor** through a gearbox, for wheels, spinners and drums;
  - a **pneumatic ram**, with your choice of ram, valve and pressure, for
    flippers, lifters, axes and spikes;
  - a **servo**, which holds positions, for legs, clamps and steering.
- **Wiring:** any actuator can follow the left or right drive, throttle,
  steering, weapon buttons 1–4 (held or toggled), or the walking gait
  (stride side, phase, swing or lift).
- **Internals:** batteries (in parallel), gas bottles (one shared supply) and
  ballast.
- **Tools:** add from a parts menu (including ready-wired assemblies such as a
  leg with hip and knee servos, an axe, a spinner or a ram spike), mirror a
  part with everything on it to the other side, duplicate, move it onto
  another part, or remove it. Click a part in the 3D view to select it.

Stats update as you build: weight, cost, drive (top speed and pushing force
for wheeled robots), battery life, and each weapon's force or stored energy
and spin-up time. There's also a full parts list with spares and rebuild time.
**Scrutineering** checks weight class, budget, size, parts below the floor,
voltage against each motor, gas for the pneumatics, wiring and battery life.
The **test bay** behind the editor lets you drive the robot against a
crash-test dummy, with live telemetry for every joint.

Starter robots: Wedgehog (wedge), Flipside (flipper), Whirlwind (undercutter),
Twin Terror (two flippers), Orb (pendulum-drive sphere), Arachnid (six-legged
walker) and Gyrodisc (full-body spinner). Saved robots appear on the fight
select screen. Designs are plain JSON, so you can copy one out to share it or
paste one in; old saves are upgraded automatically.

- **Parts:** box, wedge, flat plate, bar, cylinder/disc, cone, sphere, capsule,
  or a custom convex hull from your own points. Each one has a material
  (aluminium, mild steel, hardened steel, titanium, HDPE, polycarbonate,
  rubber, PTFE, plywood) and is either solid or a hollow shell with a wall
  thickness. Its size, position, rotation and shape offset are all editable.

  optional angle limits), or on a *slider* (with travel limits).

  - a **DC motor** through a gearbox, for wheels, spinners and drums;
  - a **pneumatic ram**, with your choice of ram, valve and pressure, for
    flippers, lifters, axes and spikes;
  - a **servo**, which holds positions, for legs, clamps and steering.

  steering, weapon buttons 1–4 (held or toggled), or the walking gait
  (stride side, phase, swing or lift).

and spin-up time. There's also a full parts list with spares and rebuild time.

crash-test dummy, with live telemetry for every joint.

Starter robots: Wedgehog (wedge), Flipside (flipper), Whirlwind (undercutter),
